construction: Pearson correlation of gene-effect profiles across 1,150 cell lines, top-8 partners per gene, r >= 0.2

join.note: registry gene/entrez keys are float-stringified upstream; normalised at the call site, NOT by editing the registry. Symbol was not used as the key.

registry_defect.problem: aliases stored float-stringified ('7105.0'); a raw Entrez id resolves 0/18,443
registry_defect.handled: normalised at the call site; registry not modified

blind_spot.documented_claim: the project's dataset plan records pan-essentials as a structural blind spot for co-dependency: no variance across lines, so nothing to correlate
blind_spot.measured: CONTRADICTED in this release. Common essentials have LARGER dependency spread and MORE partners than the rest. Their spread is largely a shared growth-rate / screen-quality axis, so they are over-connected here rather than invisible, and a common-essential edge is the type most in need of the global-axis control
blind_spot.note: a gene with no partner in this layer is UNKNOWN at this endpoint, never negative

agreement_with_existing.inferred_construction: DepMap gene-effect Pearson, top-8, r>=0.2, nearby release

sl_layer.finding: all pairs positively co-dependent -> co-requirement, not synthetic lethality; the label is wrong

viability_test.design: 5 random half-splits of cell lines; layer built on half A, scored by dependency-profile correlation on half B; controls matched on mean dependency, dependency spread and expression (training half only), 20 draws per split

mine_heldout.label: my layer, half A -> half B

transcriptional_test.design: GWPS K562 CRISPRi, per-gene robust z, matched on perturbation-strength decile x gene-responsiveness decile

limits: one release (DepMap 24Q2 Public); co-dependency values shift between releases as lines are added -- the existing layer agrees at r=0.983 but is not identical, and mixing them would mix line sets
Pearson correlation across a cancer cell line panel is not a mechanism: it cannot separate same-complex, same-pathway, shared-lineage-requirement and shared-screen-artefact
the panel is CANCER cell lines grown in 2D; a co-dependency that exists only in that context will not be marked as such here
1,336 genes dropped for incomplete profiles and the drop is not random (mean gene effect -0.1884 against -0.1432 for kept genes, MWU p 7.2e-29), so absence from this layer is unknown, not zero
expression is unknown for 9 genes; those pairs are excluded from the matched arm rather than zero-filled
the layer is SYMMETRIC and unsigned as to direction: it says A and B are needed together, not that A acts on B or that either is upstream

PAN-ESSENTIALS ARE OVER-CONNECTED, NOT INVISIBLE. The project's dataset plan says this layer is structurally blind to them; in DepMap 24Q2 Public they have LARGER dependency spread (0.283 vs 0.127) and MORE partners (96% vs 84%). Their spread is largely a shared growth-rate / screen-quality axis, so a common-essential pair is the edge type most likely to be non-specific -- see the common-essential split and the global-axis-removed arm before trusting one
it is NOT synthetic lethality. Positive co-dependency is co-requirement; SL is the opposite sign of evidence and is not measurable from this file

the transcriptional numbers in this module are a measurement of a DIFFERENT endpoint, not a grade of this layer -- and they are also a different CONTEXT: one cell line (K562) against a 1,150-line panel, so 'orthogonal endpoints' and 'orthogonal contexts' are not separated here
CRISPR gene effect is Chronos-corrected; copy number and screen-quality corrections are the pipeline's, and are inherited rather than validated here

the half-splits are held out at the level of CELL LINES, not of the whole pipeline: Chronos was fitted across all 1,150 lines before this module saw the matrix, so a shared correction could leak a little structure between halves. The held-out number is an upper bound to that extent, and the lineage-centred arm is the check that bounds it from the other side
verdict: THIS LAYER CARRIES VIABILITY INFORMATION AND ALMOST NO TRANSCRIPTIONAL INFORMATION, and the two were previously graded with one number. Held out by construction -- built on half the 1,150 DepMap 24Q2 lines, scored on the other half -- co-dependent pairs reach a raw mean dependency-profile correlation of 0.1817 on lines the build never saw, against 0.0034 for pairs matched on mean dependency, dependency spread and expression (AUC 0.926, 100% of 100 draws p<0.05 over 5 independent splits; residual imbalance p 0.15/0.0021/0.08). It survives all three falsification checks: hubness as a fourth matched covariate leaves 0.1817 vs 0.0045 (AUC 0.908); centring every held-out profile within its Oncotree lineage, which deletes all between-lineage structure, leaves 0.1707 vs 0.0047 (AUC 0.914); and projecting the 5 strongest global axes -- growth rate, screen quality, broad essentiality -- out of the held-out half leaves 0.0902 vs 0.0025 (AUC 0.757). So it is not hub, lineage or global-axis bookkeeping. It is NOT uniform across edge types: pairs of common essentials reach 0.2570 (AUC 0.961) against 0.1761 (AUC 0.924) for pairs with neither -- and the project's own dataset plan has this backwards, recording pan-essentials as a structural blind spot when in this release they carry LARGER dependency spread (0.283 vs 0.127) and MORE partners (96% vs 84%). On the transcriptional fast test the SAME pairs give 1.068x (56,403 testable cells, median p 7.99e-09, AUC 0.510) -- just over the 1.05 floor, against PPI's 1.208x -- and it barely moves with co-dependency strength (whole range 0.027 across bands) (ratios 1.059, 1.070, 1.087, 1.077 across r bands 0.20/0.25/0.30/0.40+), so the two endpoints are close to orthogonal rather than one being a weak version of the other. An AUC of 0.510 is the number to keep: the transcriptional effect is real (median p 7.99e-09, 100% of draws) and useless for deciding anything about a single pair. What little of it there is looks like shared essentiality rather than partnership -- at 30x30 bins, common-essential pairs give 1.105x against 1.043x for pairs with neither. Provenance for the pre-existing layer is recovered rather than assumed: my correlations agree with its stated values at r=0.983 and recover 70% of its pairs, so it is DepMap gene-effect Pearson from a nearby release. The `sl` layer is co-dependency mislabelled -- all 1,256 pairs are POSITIVELY correlated, which is co-requirement, the opposite sign of evidence from synthetic lethality.
